Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.driver

Interface RowCursor

All Superinterfaces:
AutoCloseable, Iterable<Map<String,Object>>, Iterator<Map<String,Object>>
@Internal public interface RowCursor extends Iterator<Map<String,Object>>, Iterable<Map<String,Object>>, AutoCloseable
Streams the rows of one read, one row at a time, while the statement stays open.

A cursor is iterated once: iterator() returns the cursor itself on the first call and refuses any later call. It moves through four states: created, open (iterating), consumed (the last row was read) and closed. hasNext() answering false closes the cursor, so a loop that runs to the end releases everything by itself; a loop left early must call close(), best through try-with-resources. 


 try (RowCursor rows = connection.cursor("select * from orders order by id")) {
     for (Map<String, Object> row : rows) {
         export(row);
     }
 }

A cursor is not thread-safe and belongs to the thread that opened it.

API Note:
Internal: driver SPI for dialect modules.
Implementation Requirements:
Rows must be in result order with columns in select order, keyed by the label as the database reports it, as for DriverSession.query(java.lang.String, java.util.List<java.lang.Object>). next() after the last row must throw NoSuchElementException; after close() it must throw IllegalStateException. hasNext() after close() answers false. close() must be idempotent and must release the statement even when an earlier step of closing failed. A failure while reading must be reported as a DriverException; the caller then closes the cursor.
